newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ground troops leave Texas for Gulf.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ground troops leave Texas for Gulf.

text.p: The first of more than 3,000 troops being deployed strengthen U.S. military forces in the Gulf flew from the Fort Hood army base in central Texas on Wednesday morning.
A total of 219 soldiers of Fort Hood's 1st Cavalry Division left the base at 10 a.m. (1500 GMT) on a commercial jet after saying goodbye to their families.
Officials said 73 more soldiers were to leave for Kuwait on a C-5 military cargo plane on Wednesday afternoon and that two flights early on Thursday would carry more than 700.
Lt. Col. Randy Schoel said the staggered deployment would be completed over the next two or three days, with each flight taking between 17 and 22 hours.
President Bill Clinton ordered the deployment to keep up the pressure on Iraq's president, Saddam Hussein.
The formal mission of the Fort Hood troops was to provide training for Kuwaiti forces but they could be used in any new military action against Iraq.
